# core/dns.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/dns.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The messages of a DNS lookup for an IPv4 address (RFC
1035): the query for a host name and the reading of the response.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and the reader
looks at no byte outside the response, whatever it holds (names are
skipped, never followed, so a pointer loop cannot hang it). Not proved:
that a query is one a resolver accepts or that the reader accepts every
response of the standard; the tests compare the query with one made by
another program. The reader takes the first A record of a response to the
one question asked, checks the id (which is all the protection against a
forged answer a plain UDP resolver gives, so use an unpredictable one),
and refuses a truncated response or one with an error code.

`import "core/dns.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`dns_query`](#dns_query) | The query for the A record of the host `name`, with the message id `id` (the 12-byte header, the question, no length prefix). |
| [`dns_query_type`](#dns_query_type) | `dns_query` for records of type `ty` (1 is A, 28 is AAAA). |
| [`dns_parse_a`](#dns_parse_a) | The IPv4 address (as `net_ip4` makes it) in the first A record of the response `msg` to a query with id `id`; `None` if the response is not a complete answer without error to that query or holds no A record. |
| [`dns_resolv_conf`](#dns_resolv_conf) | The first IPv4 `nameserver` of the text of a resolv.conf (IPv6 servers and other lines are skipped). |
| [`dns_hosts`](#dns_hosts) | The IPv4 address that the text of a hosts file (`/etc/hosts`) gives to `name`, ignoring case; lines for IPv6 addresses and comments are skipped, and the first line that names it wins. |
| [`dns_parse_aaaa`](#dns_parse_aaaa) | The IPv6 address (16 bytes, network order) in the first AAAA record of the response `msg` to an AAAA query with id `id`; `None` if the response is not a complete answer without error to that query or holds no AAAA record. |
| [`dns_ip6`](#dns_ip6) | The IPv6 address written in `t[from..to]` as groups of one to four hex digits between colons, with at most one `::` for a run of zero groups (no embedded dotted quad, no zone). |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `dns_query`

```bastio
fn dns_query(name: &Bytes, id: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires id < 65536
```

The query for the A record of the host `name`, with the message id `id`
(the 12-byte header, the question, no length prefix): `None` if `name` is
empty, longer than 253 bytes, or has an empty or over-long label.

Example:

```bastio
let name = bfrom("a.bc");
let mut bad = 1;
match dns_query(name, 4660) {
  Option::Some(q) => {
    if blen(q) == 12 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 4 && bget(q, 0) == 18 && bget(q, 1) == 52 && bget(q, 12) == 1 && bget(q, 13) == 97 && bget(q, 14) == 2 {
      bad = 0;
    }
    bfree(q);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `dns_query_type`

```bastio
fn dns_query_type(name: &Bytes, id: u64, ty: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires id < 65536 && ty < 65536
```

`dns_query` for records of type `ty` (1 is A, 28 is AAAA).

Example:

```bastio
let name = bfrom("a.b");
let mut bad = 1;
match dns_query_type(name, 4660, 28) {
  Option::Some(q) => {
    if blen(q) == 12 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 4 && bget(q, 18) == 28 {
      bad = 0;
    }
    bfree(q);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `dns_parse_a`

```bastio
fn dns_parse_a(msg: &Bytes, id: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires blen(msg) < 1073741824
```

The IPv4 address (as `net_ip4` makes it) in the first A record of the
response `msg` to a query with id `id`; `None` if the response is not a
complete answer without error to that query or holds no A record.

Example:

```bastio
// a.b -> 1.2.3.4, the answer's name a pointer to the question's.
let mut t = text_new();
text_push(&mut t, 18); text_push(&mut t, 52); text_push(&mut t, 129); text_push(&mut t, 128);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0);
text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 97); text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 98); text_push(&mut t, 0);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1);
text_push(&mut t, 192); text_push(&mut t, 12);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 60);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 4);
text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 2); text_push(&mut t, 3); text_push(&mut t, 4);
let msg = text_finish(t);
let mut bad = 1;
match dns_parse_a(msg, 4660) {
  Option::Some(ip) => { if ip == 16909060 { bad = 0; } },
  Option::None => {},
}
match dns_parse_a(msg, 4661) {
  Option::Some(ip) => { bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(msg);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `dns_resolv_conf`

```bastio
fn dns_resolv_conf(text: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

The first IPv4 `nameserver` of the text of a resolv.conf (IPv6 servers
and other lines are skipped).

Example:

```bastio
let text = bfrom("# comment\nsearch lan\nnameserver fe80::1\nnameserver 192.168.1.1 # router\nnameserver 8.8.8.8\n");
let mut bad = 1;
match dns_resolv_conf(text) {
  Option::Some(ip) => { if ip == 3232235777 { bad = 0; } },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(text);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `dns_hosts`

```bastio
fn dns_hosts(text: &Bytes, name: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

The IPv4 address that the text of a hosts file (`/etc/hosts`) gives to
`name`, ignoring case; lines for IPv6 addresses and comments are skipped,
and the first line that names it wins. `localhost` is always 127.0.0.1
(RFC 6761), file or not.

Example:

```bastio
let text = bfrom("# hosts\n::1 localhost\n10.0.0.5  Build  ci.lan # the CI box\n127.0.1.1 build\n");
let name = bfrom("CI.lan");
let local = bfrom("localhost");
let mut bad = 1;
match dns_hosts(text, name) {
  Option::Some(ip) => { if ip == 167772165 { bad = 0; } },
  Option::None => {},
}
match dns_hosts(text, local) {
  Option::Some(ip) => { if ip != 2130706433 { bad = 1; } },
  Option::None => { bad = 1; },
}
bfree(local);
bfree(name);
bfree(text);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `dns_parse_aaaa`

```bastio
fn dns_parse_aaaa(msg: &Bytes, id: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(msg) < 1073741824
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 16
```

The IPv6 address (16 bytes, network order) in the first AAAA record of the
response `msg` to an AAAA query with id `id`; `None` if the response is not
a complete answer without error to that query or holds no AAAA record.

Example:

```bastio
// a.b -> 2001:db8::1, the answer's name a pointer to the question's.
let mut t = text_new();
text_push(&mut t, 18); text_push(&mut t, 52); text_push(&mut t, 129); text_push(&mut t, 128);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0);
text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 97); text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 98); text_push(&mut t, 0);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 28); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1);
text_push(&mut t, 192); text_push(&mut t, 12);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 28); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 60);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 16);
text_push(&mut t, 32); text_push(&mut t, 1); text_push(&mut t, 13); text_push(&mut t, 184);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0);
text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 0); text_push(&mut t, 1);
let msg = text_finish(t);
let mut bad = 1;
match dns_parse_aaaa(msg, 4660) {
  Option::Some(a) => {
    if blen(a) == 16 && bget(a, 0) == 32 && bget(a, 3) == 184 && bget(a, 15) == 1 { bad = 0; }
    bfree(a);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(msg);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `dns_ip6`

```bastio
fn dns_ip6(t: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(t)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 16
```

The IPv6 address written in `t[from..to]` as groups of one to four hex
digits between colons, with at most one `::` for a run of zero groups
(no embedded dotted quad, no zone): 16 bytes in network order, or `None`.

Example:

```bastio
let t = bfrom("2001:db8::1");
let mut bad = 1;
match dns_ip6(t, 0, blen(t)) {
  Option::Some(a) => {
    if blen(a) == 16 && bget(a, 0) == 32 && bget(a, 1) == 1 && bget(a, 2) == 13 && bget(a, 3) == 184 && bget(a, 14) == 0 && bget(a, 15) == 1 { bad = 0; }
    bfree(a);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(t);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `dns_push_labels`

```bastio
fn dns_push_labels(t: &mut Vec[u8], name: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(name) >= 1 && blen(name) <= 253
```

Internal: pushes the labels of `name` (at most 253 bytes, dots between
non-empty labels of at most 63 bytes, one dot allowed at the end) and the
zero that ends them. False if `name` is not of that form (`t` then holds
part of the labels).

### `dns_skip_name`

```bastio
fn dns_skip_name(msg: &Bytes, from: u64) -> u64
  requires from <= blen(msg)
  ensures result <= blen(msg) && (result == 0 || result > from)
```

Internal: the position behind the name that starts at `from` in `msg`: a
compression pointer ends a name and is not followed. 0 if the name is
malformed or runs past the end.

### `dns_answers`

```bastio
fn dns_answers(msg: &Bytes, id: u64) -> u64
  ensures result < 65536 && (result == 0 || blen(msg) >= 12)
```

Internal: the number of answers in `msg` if it is a complete response
without error to the one question with id `id`, else 0.

### `dns_scan_a`

```bastio
fn dns_scan_a(msg: &Bytes, from: u64, cnt: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires from <= blen(msg) && cnt < 65536
```

Internal: the first A record of `cnt` answers that start at `from`.

### `dns_octet`

```bastio
fn dns_octet(t: &Bytes, at: u64, to: u64) -> u64
  requires at <= to && to <= blen(t)
  ensures result == 0 || (result / 256 >= 1 && result / 256 <= 3 && result % 256 <= 255 && at + result / 256 <= to)
```

Internal: the decimal number of at most 3 digits that starts at `at`
(below `to`) in `t`, as `digits * 256 + value`; 0 if there is none or it is
above 255. The position behind it is `at + digits`.

### `dns_dotted`

```bastio
fn dns_dotted(t: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(t)
```

Internal: the dotted-quad IPv4 address that fills `t[from..to]`.

### `dns_nameserver_line`

```bastio
fn dns_nameserver_line(t: &Bytes, ls: u64, le: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires ls <= le && le <= blen(t)
```

Internal: the address on the line `t[ls..le]` if it is `nameserver`, white
space and an IPv4 address (a comment or white space may follow).

### `dns_lower`

```bastio
fn dns_lower(c: u8) -> u8
```

Internal: the byte `c` in lower case (ASCII letters only).

### `dns_name_is`

```bastio
fn dns_name_is(t: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64, name: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(t)
```

Internal: `t[from..to]` is the same name as `name`, ignoring ASCII case.

### `dns_hosts_line`

```bastio
fn dns_hosts_line(t: &Bytes, ls: u64, le0: u64, name: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
  requires ls <= le0 && le0 <= blen(t)
```

Internal: the address of the hosts-file line `t[ls..le]` (an IPv4 address,
then names, `#` starts a comment) if `name` is one of its names.

### `dns_scan_aaaa`

```bastio
fn dns_scan_aaaa(msg: &Bytes, from: u64, cnt: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires from <= blen(msg) && cnt < 65536
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 16
```

Internal: the first AAAA record of `cnt` answers that start at `from`.

### `dns_hexval`

```bastio
fn dns_hexval(c: u8) -> u64
  ensures result <= 16
```

Internal: the value of the hex digit `c`, 16 if it is none.
